papers.title: Abrasive Water Jet Machining (AWJM) of Titanium Alloy—A Review
papers.abstract: Abrasive water jet machining (AWJM) is a non-traditional machining process that is increasingly employed for shaping hard-to-machine materials, particularly titanium (Ti)-based alloys such as Ti-6Al-4V. Owing to its non-thermal nature, AWJM enables effective material removal while minimising metallurgical damage and preserving subsurface integrity. The process performance is governed by several interacting parameters, including jet pressure, abrasive type and flow rate, nozzle traverse speed, stand-off distance, jet incident angle, and nozzle design. These parameters collectively influence key output responses such as the material removal rate (MRR), surface roughness, kerf geometry, and subsurface quality. The existing studies consistently report that the jet pressure and abrasive flow rate are directly proportional to MRR, whereas the nozzle traverse speed and stand-off distance exhibit inverse relationships. Nozzle geometry plays a critical role in jet acceleration and abrasive entrainment through the Venturi effect, thereby affecting the cutting efficiency and surface finish. Optimisation studies based on the design of the experiments identify jet pressure and traverse speed as the most significant parameters controlling the surface quality in the AWJM of titanium alloys. Recent research demonstrates the effectiveness of artificial neural networks (ANNs) for process modelling and optimisation of AWJM of Ti-6Al-4V, achieving high predictive accuracy with limited experimental data. This review highlights research gaps in artificial intelligence-based fatigue behaviour prediction, computational fluid dynamics analysis of nozzle wear mechanisms and jet behaviour, and the development of hybrid AWJM systems for enhanced machining performance.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文章是关于磨料水射流加工钛合金的综述，未聚焦于增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理对疲劳或力学性能的影响。
llm.why_not_core: This is a general review on abrasive water jet machining of titanium alloys, not specifically addressing post-processing effects on the fatigue or mechanical performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_en.motivation: To review the current state of research on abrasive water jet machining of titanium alloys.
summary_en.method: A comprehensive literature review was conducted to analyze the effects of process parameters on machining performance.
summary_en.result: Key parameters such as jet pressure and traverse speed were identified as critical for material removal rate and surface quality.
summary_en.validation: The review is based on existing studies without new experimental validation.

papers.title: Regulation Mechanism of Friction Stir Processing Parameters on Microstructure and Properties of Laser Metal Deposited TC4 Titanium Alloy
papers.abstract: To enhance the microstructure and mechanical properties of TC4 titanium alloy formed by laser metal deposition (LMD), friction stir processing (FSP) was employed to modify the surface of the as‐deposited TC4 titanium alloy. This study systematically investigates the effects of FSP parameters—rotational speed (250–1050 rpm) and travel speed (50–210 mm min −1 )—on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LMD‐formed TC4 titanium alloy. Results indicate that FSP effectively refines the coarse as‐deposited microstructure into uniform equiaxed grains, eliminates the internal defects such as porosity, and enhances phase homogeneity. Microhardness increased from 305.2 HV 1 (LMD) to a maximum of 345.2 HV 1 at 850 rpm and 210 mm min −1 . Grain refinement was confirmed by broadening XRD peaks and increased β‐phase content at higher rotational speeds. The β‐phase stabilizing element V increased from 3.8% to 5.0% with higher heat input, while Al content varied between 5.2% and 6.3% depending on thermal exposure. Wear resistance improved significantly: wear rate decreased from 5.9 × 10 −4 mm 3 N −1 m −1 (LMD) to 2.22 × 10 −4 mm 3 N −1 m −1 at 850 rpm and 210 mm min −1 . These findings validate that suitable FSP parameters can effectively tailor the microstructure and substantially enhance the mechanical properties of LMD‐formed TC4 alloy, offering a viable route for additive‐equivalent hybrid manufacturing.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了激光金属沉积TC4钛合金的摩擦搅拌加工后处理，但没有涉及疲劳性能，因此对L1方向的直接贡献有限。
llm.why_not_core: No fatigue testing or fatigue life characterization; focuses on post-processing (FSP) rather than as-built condition.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善激光金属沉积TC4钛合金的微观组织和力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 系统研究摩擦搅拌加工参数（转速和行进速度）对微观组织和性能的影响。
summary_zh.result: 摩擦搅拌加工细化晶粒、消除孔隙，显微硬度和耐磨性显著提升。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观表征和力学测试验证参数效果。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the microstructure and mechanical properties of laser metal deposited TC4 titanium alloy through friction stir processing.
summary_en.method: Systematically investigate the effects of friction stir processing parameters (rotation speed and travel speed) on microstructural evolution and mechanical performance.
summary_en.result: Friction stir processing effectively refines the coarse as-deposited microstructure, eliminates porosity, and improves microhardness and wear resistance.
summary_en.validation: Validated by microstructural characterization (XRD, SEM), microhardness testing, and wear rate measurements.
